newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SACCHI'S JOB IN PERIL AMID JEERS FROM FANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SACCHI'S JOB IN PERIL AMID JEERS FROM FANS.

text.p: Police had to escort Italian coach Arrigo Sacchi from the dressing room amid jeers from fans after Italy's disappointing performance in Wednesday's 1-0 World Cup qualifying win against Georgia.
And his future in the job looked once again in doubt as critics slammed the team's performance on Thursday.
The narrow win in Perugia did not satisfy fans still smarting from Italy's early exit from this summer's European Championship finals in England.
And it followed an equally unconvincing performance in their first qualifier, a 3-1 win away against lowly Moldova five days ago.
The Perugia crowd whistled Italy throughout the second half, even offering the celebrated "ole" for a series of passing movements by the Georgia team.
"Sacchi, Farewell", ran a front page headline in Rome sports daily "Corriere Dello Sport" on Thursday.

"Last night in Perugia, the last chapter of Sacchi's history as team coach was written...when you play two games like these ones against Georgia and Moldova, then there's no option but to turn over a new leaf," the newspaper said.

Sacchi, whose contract is worth a reported $1 million a year and not due to expire until the 1998 World Cup finals in France, told Italian television seconds after the game: "The whistles are the result of an orchestrated campaign (against us)."
"The real truth is that we've picked up three golden points," he added.
But Rome daily "La Repubblica" commented: "After a performance as worrying and poor, as inspid and cold as this one, the best comment would be silence."
The possibility of a new Italian Football Federation president in place by December has prompted speculation that Sacchi's future may be in jeopardy.
The Federation is now headed by a short term commissioner, Raffaele Pagnozzi, following the failure to elect a new chief in August in the wake of the departure of Antonio Matarrese.
Luciano Nizzola, current Italian League President and the man expected to be appointed the next Federation President, was cautious on Sacchi's future.
"Any decision...about the Italian coach will not be taken by one man alone but by the entire Federation staff. For the time being, I can't say any more...I'm not yet the new President," he said.
